correctness.rationale: For all real n>=9, four orbit-entry polynomials are obtained from the exact disjoint-triple walk-count recurrence. Exactly eleven symbolic sign/negative-discriminant facts were checked after substitution n=9+t with strictly positive rational numerators/denominators, proving a unique positive disjoint-class cubic root and all-timestep positivity of both intersecting off-diagonal classes. Scalar RK4 Taylor positivity on a symmetric positive-semidefinite Laplacian proves diagonal positivity. Direct independently enumerated adjacency powers agree on 1,845 entries for n=9,10,11. At n=8 the r=1 entry equals x^2(43x^2-480x+1200)/240000 and is -5/384 at x=5. Logs alone are not the proof; the exact symbolic identities and combinatorial induction establish infinite parameter coverage.

originality.rationale: Inspected Kneser foundational full text, Horvath general Runge-Kutta positivity full text, and full text of the SSP multistep literature. No inspected source provided the completed classical RK4 threshold on unit KG(n,3), nor global positivity of both intersecting-triple orbit entries. Prior exactly checked Johnson J(n,3) result concerns distance-one subset exchange adjacency, whereas Kneser uses disjointness; the statement is not a corollary, despite shared Johnson-scheme orbit algebra. Kneser KG(n,3) is not strongly regular; published diameter-two strongly regular graph formulas cannot cover it. Search nonappearance is not proof of priority.

value.rationale: This complete all-order threshold concerns a natural, highly symmetric but non-strongly-regular family with four intersection orbits. The nontrivial fact that intersecting nonedges remain strictly positive at all positive timesteps (with sharp order-eight counterexample), while disjoint edges undergo one irreversible sign transition, adds structural information unavailable from the usual SSP sufficient step bound. It gives a reproducible, exact benchmark for endpoint positivity in high-connectivity numerical diffusion; the parameter n is inherent to the graph rather than an arbitrary finite slice.
